facts.text: No published tolerance specific to an off-road automatic-braking stopping-distance model was found.
facts.quote: No published tolerance specific to an off-road automatic-braking stopping-distance model was found

facts.text: No exact numerical tolerances for off-road AEB were found in the reviewed standards.
facts.quote: no exact numerical tolerances for off-road AEB were found in the reviewed standards.

facts.text: EU 2022/1426 requires manufacturers to set and document their own acceptance thresholds for each model; this is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: EU 2022/1426 requires manufacturers to set and document their own acceptance thresholds per model

facts.text: UN R152 leaves validity thresholds to the manufacturer's documented method, with authority agreement; this is on-road evidence.
facts.quote: UN R152 leaves validity thresholds to the manufacturer's documented method with authority agreement.

facts.text: In practice, tolerance for the off-road automatic-braking model has to be derived from the safety margin and measurement uncertainty.
facts.quote: In practice the tolerance has to be derived from the safety margin and the measurement uncertainty.

facts.text: If the ISO 21815-3 risk area leaves X metres of margin, the combined model-form, numerical and input uncertainty must be demonstrably smaller than X; this is a design principle, not a published numerical tolerance.
facts.quote: if the ISO 21815-3 risk area leaves X metres of margin, the model-form uncertainty plus numerical and input uncertainty must be demonstrably smaller than X. This is a design principle, not a published number.

facts.text: A model accuracy criterion is not a system safety criterion.
facts.quote: A model accuracy criterion is not a system safety criterion.

facts.text: A simulator can be demonstrably imperfect yet conservative enough for a particular decision.
facts.quote: A simulator can be demonstrably imperfect yet conservative enough for a particular decision

facts.text: A simulator can have low average error while being dangerously optimistic around the collision boundary.
facts.quote: have low average error while being dangerously optimistic around the collision boundary.

facts.text: FDA's threshold logic and FAA's treatment of safety margins support decision-oriented rather than goodness-of-fit-oriented validation.
facts.quote: FDA's threshold logic and the FAA's treatment of safety margins both support decision-oriented rather than goodness-of-fit-oriented validation.

facts.text: Recommended validation quantities for off-road automatic braking are detection probability and false-negative rate by condition, false-positive or unnecessary-braking rate, range and relative-speed error distributions, intervention-time error, brake-pressure and deceleration histories, stopping-distance error, residual impact-speed error, and frequency of model residuals near decision boundaries. These are recommended metrics, not published off-road thresholds.
facts.quote: detection probability and false-negative rate by condition, false-positive or unnecessary-braking rate, range and relative-speed error distributions, intervention-time error, brake-pressure and deceleration histories, stopping-distance error, residual impact-speed error
